Property expenses declined by 6.1% to SEK 4,378 million, reflecting successful cost control measures, digitalisation initiatives, and the reduced size of the portfolio following unit sales.
Consequently, net operating income increased by 2.6% to SEK 11,475 million, elevating the LTM net operating income margin to 72.1% from 70.3% in 2024.

verified_key_information_units.information: Country-specific investment property fair value developments: Sweden +0.8% (SEK 717m) from rental performance; Germany +1.2% (SEK 926m) despite privatisation strategy shift; Denmark +7.2% (SEK 4,643m) from ownership market strength; Czechia +6.7% (SEK 1,856m) from rental growth; Netherlands +5.4% (SEK 1,424m) with privatisation as highest-and-best use; Norway -2.7% (SEK -382m) from buy-to-let supply increase; UK -0.4% (SEK -20m) from yield stabilisation; Poland +4.1% (SEK 173m) and Finland +4.3% (SEK 161m) from rental growth and rent reversion.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: MD&A: Investment Properties, Country Fair Value Development section

verified_key_information_units.information: Liquidity and financing: Heimstaden Bostad completed SEK 59,500 million financing (refinancings and new financings); liability management in January 2025 issued SEK 750 million senior unsecured floating rate notes and EUR 430 million/400 million fixed rate notes while tendering existing maturities; interest expenses of SEK 6,536 million (average rate 3.43% vs 3.01% in 2024); interest coverage ratio improved to 2.0x (1.9x); net loan-to-value decreased to 52.2% (56.4%); unutilised credit facilities of SEK 23,449 million at parent level.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: MD&A: Funding section, Interest Expenses, Liability Management, Alternative Performance Measures

candidate_sentences.text: Financing activities remained a focal point, with the group advancing its deleveraging trajectory through targeted privatisation sales and liability management exercises that successfully extended debt maturities.
Net loan-to-value decreased to 52.2% from 56.4% a year earlier, while the interest coverage ratio improved to 2.0 times.
Total interest-bearing liabilities stood at SEK 175,227 million, with an average interest rate of 3.4% and substantial unutilised credit facilities of SEK 23,449 million providing liquidity headroom.

The group completed approximately SEK 59,500 million in refinancing and new funding transactions, including green bond issuances and bank financing, maintaining access to favourable capital market terms despite shifting macroeconomic conditions.

verified_key_information_units.information: Material post-reporting-period events: December 2025 arbitration award in favour of Heimstaden confirmed no breach of Heimstaden Bostad Shareholders' Agreement; January 2025 issuance of EUR 500 million perpetual hybrid maturity by Heimstaden Bostad replaced EUR 500 million perpetual hybrid resetting in April 2026.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: MD&A: Q4 Highlights (arbitration), Funding section (hybrid bond)

candidate_sentences.text: In legal matters, an arbitral tribunal ruled in favour of the company in the dispute initiated by shareholder Alecta, confirming no breach of the shareholders agreement.

verified_key_information_units.information: Sustainability performance: weather-corrected energy intensity reduced 10% to 148 kWh/m² (exceeding 2% target); GHG emissions reduced 14.2% against 2020 baseline (on track for 42% reduction by 2030); EU Taxonomy-aligned revenue at 22% (26% in 2024) and capex at 18% (22% in 2024); green assets valued at approximately SEK 76 billion supported green bond issuance of SEK 13,767 million in FY25; sustainability-linked loans of SEK 5,818 million all met KPIs (Sustainalytics Negligible Risk, SBTi emission target achievement).
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Sustainability Report: Highlights, E1 sections, EU Taxonomy tables

candidate_sentences.text: Business developments were marked by continued progress on sustainability commitments and strategic investor relations.

The subsidiary received Sustainalytics Negligible ESG risk for the third consecutive year, while energy intensity improved by 10% on a weather-corrected basis and greenhouse gas emissions fell 14.2% against the 2020 baseline.
